title: Banking In India Scheduled Commercial Banks
definition: Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) in India comprise all banks included in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, 1934, satisfying criteria of minimum paid-up capital and reserves, and ensuring operations do not adversely affect depositors' interests.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC Prelims (RBI Act provisions, bank categorization, priority sector lending, capital adequacy norms) and GS Paper III Mains (financial inclusion, banking sector reforms, NPAs, bad bank, digital banking).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Banking In India Scheduled Commercial Banks.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of monetary policy, financial intermediaries, and the central bank.
